title: FIX-724 & FIX-730: Ticket Context and Scout Artifacts Walkthrough
description: This tour covers two helix-cli ticket runs: FIX-724 (a UI bug where a failed ticket incorrectly showed a successful run with no merge options) and FIX-730 (a vague inquiry about second runs, recurring failures, and failure reports). Neither ticket required changes to CLI source code — instead, the agent materialized ticket context files and a scout analysis confirming the CLI is a thin REST API client and the root causes live server-side. This tour walks through the ticket context files and scout artifacts in the order they inform the investigation.

steps.description: This is the materialized ticket context for FIX-724 ('Another bug'). The description references FIX-712 and BLD-680, and three screenshot attachments show the UI inconsistency: the ticket status shows Failed while the run detail page shows successful with no merge options available. This file is generated by the Helix agent to give it full ticket context before scouting or making changes. The referenced tickets (FIX-712 and BLD-680) are materialized under `.helix-refs/` for cross-ticket artifact inspection.
steps.title: FIX-724: Ticket Context

steps.description: Two tickets are cross-referenced: BLD-680 ('Egress Lockdown ⑥ — Account-scoped NetSuite egress', FAILED) and FIX-712 ('Missing Run Fix And other bugs', DEPLOYED). The agent materialized their artifacts under `.helix-refs/` so it can inspect prior fix context. FIX-712 in particular is directly relevant — it was a previous fix for missing run and UI bugs, and its DEPLOYED status confirms those changes are already live. This cross-referencing pattern helps the agent avoid re-implementing already-deployed fixes.
steps.title: FIX-724: Referenced Tickets Section

steps.description: This is the materialized ticket context for FIX-730 ('Yet Another Bug'). The description is vague: it asks why there was a second run, why it keeps failing, and why failure is being reported. No attachments are provided. This ticket's scope is unclear from the description alone, which is why the scout analysis (next steps) is critical — the agent must determine whether this is a CLI-level issue or a server-side issue before making any changes.
steps.title: FIX-730: Ticket Context

steps.description: The scout reference map records which CLI files are relevant to the ticket and why. Four files are identified: `src/tickets/rerun.ts` (triggers reruns via POST /api/tickets/{id}/rerun), `src/tickets/continue.ts` (triggers continuation runs with a continuationContext field), `src/tickets/get.ts` (displays all runs with status and timestamps), and `src/lib/http.ts` (HTTP retry logic with exponential backoff for 429/500/502/503/504). The key conclusion in the 'unknowns' section is that the CLI is a thin REST client — run lifecycle and failure logic live server-side, not here.
steps.title: FIX-730: Scout Reference Map

steps.description: The facts section captures important invariants discovered during scouting: both rerun and continue commands POST to the same endpoint (rerun passes no extra context, continue passes continuationContext), the HTTP client retries up to 3 times with exponential backoff, terminal statuses are failed/error/cancelled/completed/succeeded, and there is no database or ORM in this repo. The unknowns confirm the ticket does not reference any CLI-specific behavior and CLI changes are unlikely to be needed. This gates the agent from making unnecessary or incorrect source changes.
steps.title: FIX-730: Scout Facts and Unknowns

steps.description: The scout summary synthesizes the reference map into a human-readable analysis. It confirms the CLI is context-only for FIX-730: the two relevant commands (hlx tickets rerun, hlx tickets continue) both delegate to the server endpoint, the HTTP client's own retry logic is separate from server-level run retries, and run history display via hlx tickets get shows status/timestamps but does not control run behavior. The summary table maps each file to its relevance, and the artifact inputs section records what the agent read to reach this conclusion. No source code changes are warranted in helix-cli for this ticket.
steps.title: FIX-730: Scout Summary — Context-Only Verdict

steps.description: Both FIX-724 and FIX-730 conclude without CLI source modifications. FIX-724's UI inconsistency (failed ticket showing successful run, no merge options) is a server-side or frontend rendering issue — the CLI merely displays what the server returns. FIX-730's questions about second runs and recurring failures point to server-side run orchestration logic. The helix-cli codebase's major code paths (rerun, continue, get, HTTP retry) remain intact and unchanged. The scout artifacts serve as a durable record of the agent's reasoning, ensuring future runs or reviewers can audit why no CLI changes were made.
steps.title: Summary: Clean Codebase Confirmation
